step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Visual & Audio Transcription: FanFight architecture uses Mobile & Web Users connecting via API Gateway to AWS Lambda functions, which interact with MongoDBAtlas as the operational database. External Game APIs push score/point changes to trigger Lambda functions that write change data into Amazon S3. Post-match events are triggered by CloudWatch to export MongoDB match data into S3. From S3, Amazon EMR runs Spark jobs to process leaderboard ranks and estimated winnings, writing results back to MongoDBAtlas. Data from S3 is also loaded into Amazon Redshift for analytics on promotions, free entries, and couponing.
2. Node Identification: Standardized to allowed vocabulary (UserConsumerWebMobile, ApiGateway, CloudWatch, ThirdParty, Lambda, MongoDBAtlas, S3, EMR, RedShift).
3. Flow Construction: Segregated into user API requests (flow 0), live score updates (flow 1), post-match export (flow 2), EMR leaderboard calculation (flow 3), and Redshift analytics (flow 4).

graph.name: FanFight Daily Fantasy Sports Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture handles 1.5M new monthly registered users and 500k active users per match. Features real-time score ingestion, serverless API execution, batch leaderboard processing with EMR Spark, and analytics with Redshift.

nodes.name: Mobile & Web Users
nodes.notes: Over 1.5M registered users, around 500k active team creators per match.

nodes.name: API
nodes.notes: Receives user requests from mobile apps and web frontend.

nodes.name: CW
nodes.notes: Provides automated triggers (events) after match starts to ingest data.

nodes.name: GAME APIs
nodes.notes: External sports score APIs sending real-time point and score updates.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless backend functions processing API requests and score events.

nodes.name: MongoDB
nodes.notes: Primary database storing user teams, match details, and computed leaderboards.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central storage/data lake storing score changes and match historical data.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Executes Spark jobs to compute ranks and estimated winnings.

nodes.name: REDSHIFT
nodes.notes: Data warehouse for analytics on free entries and coupon targeting.

edges.notes: Users send API requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway triggers backend Lambda functions.
Lambda reads and writes user team data to MongoDB.
Game APIs trigger Lambda whenever scores or points change.
Lambda stores detected score changes directly into S3.
CloudWatch triggers Lambda after a match starts.
Match-related data from MongoDB is backed up and stored in S3.
EMR Spark jobs read raw match data from S3.
EMR writes computed user rankings and winnings back into MongoDB.
Data from S3 is loaded into Redshift for business analytics.
